headline: Most of the 30 briefs say fans buy the city before the crest. It is a hypothesis to test, not a finding.
thesis: Most of the 30 briefs read their fans the same way: city first, roster second, from the area code and the ward to the county gym and the borough. That read comes from desk research, not sales data or fan surveys, so test it before building on it. The 2026 reshuffle left about a third of the league selling a new face and another third selling none. What lasts for Nike Basketball is the team, the uniform system Nike makes for every club and Nike's own archives. Climate and the local calendar, not the standings, set the product mix. The north needs deep-winter layers, and the Bay and Portland need a fog-and-rain layer. Sun Belt heat flips the calendar. Diaspora gift windows run from Black Friday to Three Kings Day, Orthodox Christmas and Lunar New Year. Nike earns the right to sell a city's codes only by paying and crediting the people who own them. Those people run from Albina and Roxbury to Oak Cliff, Little Haiti and San Antonio's West Side. Have the Portland team run that as one repeatable partner system across the league, not 30 one-off capsules.

themes.title: The area code is the new jersey
themes.insight: In 20 briefs, the surest graphic without a player on it is a local number or map. The list: 404/678/770, 112 ZIPs, 216 vs 330, the 313, DC's eight wards and 202, New Orleans ward numerals, the 901, 416/905, 405/918/580, the Clippers' six codes, 612/651/218, 92 Indiana counties, the 407, the 916 and Phoenix's Avenues-and-Streets grid. Fans use them to say which side of a city or state they're from, which a skyline or mascot can't.
themes.implication: Build one league-wide 'Codes' template: numeral type, a side-hit cap, a kids tee and a heavyweight hoodie under the local tax line. Each market fills it with its own codes and a local artist's lettering. Drop each market on its own date, not in one window. The first run is 202 Day Feb 2, 216 Day Feb 16, 313 Day Mar 13, 404 Day Apr 4, 405 Day Apr 5, 407 Day Apr 7 and 416 Day Apr 16. Then come 504 Day May 4, 612 Day Jun 12, 901 Day Sep 1 and 916 Day Sep 16. Only 404 Day and 407 Day are planned in the briefs, so confirm the others are recognized locally before treating them as holidays. Sell it as evergreen volume with the team mark as a secondary hit. The briefs expect these lines to outsell player product in reset markets and to deepen it in contenders. That protects reset markets from roster swings.

themes.title: Winter is the real uniform, in two weights
themes.insight: From October to March, the cold-market dossiers describe one outfit: a jersey over a hoodie under a shell (DC's season is shorter). It covers Boston's nor'easters, the New York and Philadelphia winter, Chicago's lake wind, Detroit's seven-month outerwear season, Minnesota's skyway walk, Toronto's 'Winter Blackout', Utah's inversion and Denver's Front Range swings. The Bay's 50-degree fog nights and Portland's wet Big Dark need a different spec: a light, water-resistant shoulder layer, not insulation.
themes.implication: Run one layer platform in two tiers, applied by metro so both New York teams share one. The deep-winter tier is heavyweight fleece, an insulated shell, an oversized jersey cut to fit over a hoodie and a knit beanie. The shoulder tier for the Bay and Portland is a packable shell, a quarter-zip and light fleece. Finish each with the city's material story: Cream City brick, Hulett truss linings, Mill City flour-sack cream, inversion gray, fog gray, Rip City reflective. Re-merchandise existing Storm-FIT and Therma-FIT now, and land the hero shells for FW27.

themes.title: The Sun Belt runs an inverted calendar
themes.insight: In Miami, Orlando, Phoenix, Houston, Dallas, San Antonio and New Orleans, the dossiers write the spec around ventilation, sun, 3 p.m. downpours and arena air-conditioning, and the outdoor season is the NBA's offseason. Los Angeles (both teams), Sacramento's triple-digit summers and humid Atlanta, Charlotte and Memphis run the same way. August back-to-school, timed to Texas and Florida tax-free weekends, is a top-three retail month there, just as the northern markets hit their annual low.
themes.implication: Make mesh, satin, linen-look and UPF shooting shirts the Sun Belt hero, not a cut-down winter line. Add packable rain shells for Florida and the Gulf. Ship an August youth pack (tee, mesh short, sub-$100 shoe) before the tax-free weekends.

themes.title: The reshuffle made return nights local tentpoles
themes.insight: The Oct 7 live-verified League Pulse confirms five 2026 moves. Giannis went from Milwaukee to Miami, Jaylen Brown from Boston to Philadelphia, Ja Morant from Memphis to Portland (traded June 29), Kawhi Leonard from the Clippers to Toronto and LaMelo Ball from Charlotte to Minnesota. LeBron James's move to Philadelphia, like Ball's, is in the verified league calendar. Dated so far: Giannis meets Milwaukee Nov 18 in Miami and returns to Fiserv Forum Jan 28, Brown plays at TD Garden Jan 21, Ball is back in Charlotte Feb 15 and LeBron plays at the Lakers on Christmas. Still undated: the Sixers' home opener against Cleveland, the Portland-Memphis and Toronto-Clippers games and Leonard's Toronto home debut. Each move left a jersey closet behind. The briefs agree these nights sell gratitude and the city, never the departed star.
themes.implication: Give each departing market (Milwaukee, Boston, Memphis, the Clippers, Charlotte, Cleveland) an undated, player-free 'thank you, city' piece. Add a re-stitch or patch kit for jerseys fans already own, like Milwaukee's Keep the Jersey or the Clippers' closet rework. In arriving markets, stock name-and-number deep at the opener and release local pieces only as wins come, the way Philadelphia's 'Earn Philly' plan does. Lock a return-night drop only once the date is on the published schedule.

themes.title: Nike makes the jersey, but often not the face
themes.insight: Minnesota's Edwards and Ball, Portland's Lillard, Washington's Trae Young, Indiana's Haliburton, Philadelphia's Iverson, Embiid and Brown, and Charlotte's new core all sit outside Nike's athlete roster. Curry's next shoe deal is open, and rivals hold Clyde, Marathon Monday and the Celtics' practice facility. Nike owns the uniform system outright, plus Specter for eight heritage clubs: Celtics, Lakers, Warriors, Knicks, 76ers, Kings, Pistons and Hawks. It also owns archive stories no rival can tell: Penny in Orlando and Memphis, Carter's purple era in Toronto, Converse in Boston, Philadelphia and Charlotte, and the AF1 'Uptown' in New York.
themes.implication: Plan these markets team-first and archive-first. Let whole-roster jersey walls, Specter and City Edition moments and Nike-family heritage capsules (Penny pinstripes, purple dino, Converse dynasty-era high-tops) carry the story. Save athlete-led product for the Nike faces who do play there: Giannis, LeBron, Wembanyama, Booker, Tatum, Doncic and Converse-signed Gilgeous-Alexander. Flagg is a New Balance athlete, so Dallas is a team-first market too.

themes.title: Holiday is plural
themes.insight: The richest gift calendars in the corpus aren't the US retail calendar. Miami has Noche Buena, Soup Joumou and Three Kings, Boricua Orlando runs Navidad a Reyes and Denver's Serbian fans keep Orthodox Christmas. Lunar New Year matters in the Bay, Brooklyn and Toronto, Diwali and Carnival in Toronto, Ramadan and Eid in Dearborn, and Fiesta in San Antonio. The briefs keep warning that these communities want to co-design, not receive a translated tee.
themes.implication: In these markets, extend holiday allocation and gift boxes from Black Friday through Jan 7. Write product Spanish-first or Kreyol-first where the community leads. Sign co-designers a season ahead so the 2027 heritage capsules are authored, not adapted.

themes.title: In the sign-painting markets, lettering is the product
themes.insight: Hand lettering is the shared design language of Memphis, LA's rotulos and serigraphs, San Antonio's West Side, Houston's pinstripers and multilingual sign painters, Orlando's OBT signage, Phoenix's Van Buren neon and New Orleans' hand-painted craft. In these seven markets the letterform carries the local identity. A generic Nike font on a team color reads as an outsider's product.
themes.implication: Commission a named local letterer in each market to draw the city's wordmarks, numerals and Codes-template type. Print them on in-line blanks through the quick-turn lane. Pay and credit them on the league co-author model in the Portland principles, not a separate deal.

themes.title: Tax codes and family size set the price
themes.insight: The retail dossiers set hard price ceilings from local rules and households. New York's clothing exemption stops at $110, Massachusetts' line sits at $175 and Texas's tax-free weekend covers items under $100. Oklahoma's statewide buyer shops under $100, and Memphis's tee sits at $35-$50. Utah, Sacramento, San Antonio and the Clippers buy for families of four or five, youth jerseys first.
themes.implication: Ladder each market's assortment against its own tax line and family math. That means a hero hoodie under $110 in New York, swingmans and jackets under $175 in Massachusetts and sub-$100 sets for Texas and Oklahoma. In the statewide and rebuild markets, go youth-first on jersey depth and add family-pack tees.

clusters.name: Heirloom Dynasties
clusters.description: The league's global heritage brands: 18 banners, six banners, 17 Lakers titles, the Knicks' 1973-to-2026 bookend and the Warriors' four-title run. Fandom is inherited like a family crest, tourists and global fans add volume, and every roster is judged against the lineage. Four of the five wear Specter this season.
clusters.playbook: Let heritage and the uniform system carry national volume: ring night, Specter, banners, Showtime, the Bay Bridge logo. Put the creative risk in the neighborhoods, not the skyline. That means borough and area-code doors in New York, Eastside serigraphs in LA, Roxbury and Dorchester in Boston, Madison Street in Chicago and Oakland first in the Bay. Launch in the neighborhood door the same day as the arena, leave core uniforms alone, and use Christmas and playoff nights as the global stages.

clusters.name: Diaspora Metros
clusters.description: Big, diaspora-majority metros with a new star or a playoff roster: Giannis in Miami, LeBron and Brown in Philadelphia, Leonard in Toronto, Wembanyama in San Antonio, Durant and Sengun in Houston. The jersey wall moves the volume, and multilingual community calendars give the depth. Those calendars define the cluster, not the standings: Detroit, Oklahoma City and Cleveland contend from other clusters.
clusters.playbook: Stock deep at the opener and through the holidays, in every size and tier. Save the hyper-local pieces for earned moments: wins, playoff rounds, Fiesta, White Hot nights. Build each community's capsule with that community, on its own calendar: Cuban, Haitian and Venezuelan Miami, North Fifth Street Philly, Toronto's Diwali-to-Carnival year, San Antonio's West Side, Southwest Houston. Pre-produce playoff fast-turn kits with local printers, because these markets are likely to play into May.

clusters.name: Great Lakes Shift Workers
clusters.description: Cold, blue-collar markets where trust is earned: the 313, the 216 and 330, Cream City, 92 county gyms. Fans prize effort over flash, punish hype and outsider pity, and buy heavyweight layers through a suburban mall ring.
clusters.playbook: Talk like a shift, not a scoreboard. Make heavyweight fleece and shells the hero, with grit-over-polish graphics in stencil, gig-poster ink and steel. Rotate paid local makers so the product reads as made here, not as Portland's idea of the Rust Belt. Price for value, sell along I-94, I-75 and the outlet corridors, and time drops to December gifting, MLK Day and the playoff run, not the Lions, Browns or Colts fall.

clusters.name: Statewide Loyalists
clusters.description: Markets whose fan base is a whole state or region: Oklahoma, Utah, Colorado, Minnesota, Oregon, the Sacramento Valley. Some share the market with other major-league teams, and only Oklahoma City is a true one-team state. Fans are loyal, family-sized, value-minded and allergic to hype or condescension. Oklahoma City, Denver and Minnesota are contenders running a value ladder, Utah and Sacramento are rebuilds selling identity, and Portland sits in between.
clusters.playbook: Sell the state, not the skyline: state-outline and multi-area-code lines, youth-first jersey ladders and family packs, sold through big-box stores, malls and highway-corridor pop-ups (I-15 Saturdays, I-5 regional doors). Contenders run the value ladder next to deep player stock and playoff fast-turn: Loud City, Jokic moments, Edwards-Ball. Rebuilds lead with identity and family gifting. Add a few credited artist drops from each city's taste districts for credibility, and take climate cues from the layer and Sun Belt themes market by market. Portland is the home lab for this cluster's playbook.

clusters.name: City-Before-Crest Culture Capitals
clusters.description: Black-led design capitals (go-go DC, hip-hop Atlanta, brass-band New Orleans, Memphis rap and jookin) where the city's own culture runs far hotter than its team fandom. That fandom arrives in spikes after rebuilds or losing seasons.
clusters.playbook: Plan about two-thirds city-first product with a secondary team mark, and one-third player and team product. Drop on the city's own dates (404 Day, Mardi Gras, MLK Day, Labor Day, second-line Sundays), not national windows. Lead every program with paid institutions and creators who own the culture: go-go bands, AUC, brass bands, Memphis rap artists, Caribbean Brooklyn. Hold uniform ideas for 2027-28 and later, after partners have co-authored them.

clusters.name: Sun Belt Arrival Cities
clusters.description: Orlando, Phoenix, Dallas and Charlotte: sprawling, car-bound Sun Belt metros, transplant-rich and Latino-heavy. They have prove-it or reset rosters, little national TV, a tourist or souvenir shopper next to the local one, and a calendar the heat turns upside down.
clusters.playbook: Separate the local from the souvenir: locals-only identity drops (407, Los Suns, Desde la Cliff, 704) next to a simple wordmark lane for visitors. Launch where taste is set (Oak Cliff, Roosevelt Row, Parramore, NoDa and the West End), then roll value-tiered volume out to suburban malls and outlets. Lead with Nike-owned heritage where it exists, like Penny pinstripes and the Hive, and build Spanish-first co-design programs for Hispanic Heritage Month 2027.

clusters.name: Second Team in a Two-Team Town
clusters.description: The Clippers and the Nets share a media market with a bigger, older brand: the Lakers and the champion Knicks. Their fans define themselves by neighborhood and by not being the other team. Both have the league's thinnest fandom this season, after a starless Clippers reset and a 20-62 Nets rebuild. Both also have real footprints: Inglewood, the South Bay, Long Beach and the SGV, and Brooklyn's Caribbean, Black and Asian neighborhoods.
clusters.playbook: Design for the footprint, not the metro. For the Clippers, that's Inglewood sign letters, the six LA codes and South Bay Filipino and Pacific Islander hoops. For the Nets, it's Kings County, Caribbean Brooklyn and Sunset Park. Never mock the big brother. Win the shared nights instead, like the Clippers' House Rules on Lakers-at-Dome nights. Keep units modest and youth-first, rework the closets left by departed stars, and hold uniform ideas for 2027-28 builds co-authored with local partners.

tentpoles.window: Oct 20-27, 2026: opening night Oct 20 on NBC, then opening week
tentpoles.moment: Opening night tripleheader and opening week: Boston at Detroit, Philadelphia at New York for Knicks ring night, and Oklahoma City at San Antonio in a West finals rematch
tentpoles.play: Nationally, lead with the champion's ring night and the new-look Sixers, both told as Specter-era stories. Locally, run 'Clock In' graphics in Detroit, the 1973/2026 rafter tee in New York, and 'Built Here' and the returning Fiesta-stripe City Edition in Oklahoma City and San Antonio. Restock jersey walls in opening week for the Luka era in LA, Flagg in Dallas and the whole-roster Lillard-Morant wall in Portland. Cleveland's 'gratitude, then the Cavs' LeBron beat runs at the Sixers' home opener against the Cavaliers (date to confirm) and at their East Group B Cup meeting, not in January.

tentpoles.window: Group play Oct 30-Nov 27, 2026 (Fridays, plus Tue Nov 24 and Wed Nov 25). Quarterfinals Dec 4-5, home semifinals Dec 8-9, final Dec 11 at Hinkle Fieldhouse
tentpoles.moment: Emirates NBA Cup: two home Cup nights per market, then the first knockouts outside Las Vegas
tentpoles.play: Each team plays four group games, only two at home, so every market gets two home-Cup drops on its own dates. The Oct 30 home teams include Washington, Indiana, Toronto, Boston, Minnesota, Phoenix, Dallas, San Antonio, the Clippers and Portland (confirm the rest from each schedule; Utah doesn't play that night). Stitch the national 'Cup Nights' story each week from whoever is home: Atlanta's Pac-Man heritage, the Clippers' Inglewood sign-letter launch, Milwaukee fish-fry Fridays, Denver's artist-print pilot, Oklahoma's Cup hoodie. Hold 48-hour knockout hoodies on pre-approved blanks for quarterfinal and home-semifinal markets, with Minnesota's ready-swap pipeline as the template. Make Hinkle the national Dec 11 story: Indiana as the home of the game, with or without the Pacers. Sell a maple-and-navy 'Fieldhouse Winter' layer and a 92-county 'Sectional' tee there.

tentpoles.window: Select 2026-27 games, dates to be announced (collection on sale since the Sept 9 reveal)
tentpoles.moment: Specter nights: the first Specter game in each of the eight heritage markets
tentpoles.play: Run one league-wide Specter rollout, keyed to each club's first Specter game once the schedule is out. Tell a national 'heritage, re-cut' story, with a local layer in each of the eight markets. Sacramento and Atlanta have few other national hooks, so they get full local programs. Sacramento puts Specter at the front of the team store and DOCO with a licensed Arco-era tee beside it. Atlanta pairs it with its red-and-gold and Pac-Man heritage on home nights. In Boston, Los Angeles, Golden State, New York, Philadelphia and Detroit, it rides alongside ring night, Christmas and the opener.

tentpoles.window: Black Friday, Nov 27, 2026, to Orthodox Christmas, Jan 7, 2027, with Noche Buena Dec 24, Soup Joumou Jan 1 and Three Kings Jan 6
tentpoles.moment: The plural holiday: US gifting plus diaspora gift calendars
tentpoles.play: Nationally, youth jersey gift boxes and family bundles. Locally, stretch allocation and the story to each community's own date. That means Cuban, Haitian and Latin gift sets in Miami, Navidad a Reyes boxes in Orlando and Orthodox Christmas Jokic gifts in Denver. Sacramento and Utah get Valley gift ladders, and Oak Cliff and San Antonio get Mexican-American family packs.

tentpoles.moment: Christmas Day: a Spurs-Knicks Finals rematch, Heat at Celtics, LeBron's return with the 76ers at the Lakers, Thunder at Timberwolves and Nuggets at Warriors
tentpoles.play: The national play is the five-game showcase, with the champion at noon. Locally: the Game 4 'Back Page' gift box in New York, a Giannis-Heat vs. Boston rivalry tee, a Lakers 'thank-you, then the new era' watch-party program, Mill City Christmas in Minneapolis and a Christmas-night crab-feed poster tee in the Bay.

tentpoles.window: Jan 18, 2027 (NBC/Peacock MLK Day quadrupleheader), with programs running MLK week through February
tentpoles.moment: MLK Day: Pistons at Cavaliers, 76ers at Hawks, Timberwolves at Knicks, Rockets vs. Grizzlies, and the start of Black History Month programs league-wide
tentpoles.play: Lead with community funding and access, not product: Atlanta's Beloved Community program, a Karamu House capsule in Cleveland, Memphis's partner program near the National Civil Rights Museum and Third Ward heritage in Houston. In February, co-authored Black history capsules follow: Russell's Boston, Brooklyn Firsts, West End Charlotte, Harlem's Rens, Chicago's AfriCOBRA lineage, DC go-go and Albina in Portland.

tentpoles.window: Brown's first return to TD Garden Jan 21, Giannis back in Milwaukee Jan 28 after a first meeting in Miami Nov 18, and Ball in Charlotte Feb 15. Portland vs. Memphis and Toronto vs. the Clippers are still to be dated
tentpoles.play: Nationally, these are the season's most-watched storylines. Locally, sell the city and gratitude, never the departed star: Milwaukee's 'Champions City' 2021 piece, a Boston-Philadelphia rivalry archive and Charlotte's new-core night for Miller and Knueppel. Memphis and the Clippers get 'thank you, city' pieces on their Morant and Leonard nights, while Portland and Toronto sell the welcome. Cleveland's LeBron beat sits in October-November with the opener.

tentpoles.window: Feb 6, 2027 for Lunar New Year (Year of the Goat) and Feb 9 for Mardi Gras, with king cake season from Jan 6
tentpoles.moment: Lunar New Year and Carnival season
tentpoles.play: Partner-designed Year of the Goat pieces belong where Asian American fans are core business, not a theme night: the Bay, Brooklyn's Sunset Park, Toronto, Flushing, Koreatown LA, Sacramento. In New Orleans, time the Twelfth Night pack to king cake, not tourist purple-green-gold.

tentpoles.window: From the Presidents' Day quadrupleheader on Feb 15, 2027 to All-Star Weekend in Phoenix, Feb 19-21
tentpoles.play: Tell the national All-Star story from Phoenix street level: a locals-first 'Made on Roosevelt' pop-up with Valley artists, Booker-led volume, Los Suns and the Mercury's women's line. Other markets localize with home watch parties and 'our All-Star' tees on in-line blanks for their selected players. Hold quick-turn slots at the trade deadline (Feb 11) for any arriving player.

tentpoles.window: 404 Day Apr 4, 407 Day Apr 7, 414 Day Apr 14 if it's recognized locally, late-April Fiesta San Antonio (2027 dates to confirm), then the Play-In Apr 13-16
tentpoles.moment: Spring city days: area-code days and Fiesta
tentpoles.play: Use local identity days as the spring bridge into the playoffs. Atlanta gets the 404 Day chapter of its area-code capsule, Orlando a locals-only 407 Day drop and San Antonio a Fiesta-stripe drop with medal-pin caps. Milwaukee gets a 414 drop if local partners confirm the day. Other markets' code days fall on their own dates from the Codes calendar (313 Day Mar 13 in Detroit, 216 Day Feb 16 in Cleveland, 504 Day May 4 in New Orleans), not in this window.

tentpoles.window: Apr 17 or 18, 2027 (playoffs begin; confirm) through the June Finals
tentpoles.play: Nationally, round tees and caps. Locally, each contender gets pre-approved 48-hour clinch kits from local licensed printers. Think Loud City blue-outs, White Hot Linen, Overtime in Detroit, Unfinished Business in Cleveland, Clutch City red-outs, Rip City red, Knicks maker-series playoff tees and a Fiesta-plus-playoffs stripe in San Antonio.

tentpoles.window: '77-at-50 on Jun 5, 2027 and Juneteenth on Jun 19, alongside the Finals and the late-June draft (date to confirm)
tentpoles.moment: Portland's 1977 title at 50, Juneteenth and Pride
tentpoles.play: Portland's '77-at-50 reissue is archive-exact, sold by raffle and co-authored with Albina. It's the one heritage moment Nike can tell from its own hometown. Juneteenth pieces in Houston's Third Ward and Pride capsules co-made with local partners (Brooklyn with the Liberty, Toronto's Blockorama) run alongside.

tentpoles.window: July to August 2027: park circuits, Kobe Day on Aug 24 and back-to-school tax-free weekends (confirm state dates)
tentpoles.play: Nationally, a park-court performance line. Locally, the summer leagues and courts each market already owns: Rucker and Dyckman in New York, the Drew in LA, Goodman League in DC, BNBL in Boston, Miami's park courts, Eastlake night courts in Phoenix and Irving Park in Portland. Ship Sun Belt youth packs before the Texas and Florida tax-free weekends. Run the 8/24 muralist series as its own estate-approved Kobe calendar.

tentpoles.window: Hispanic Heritage Month, Sep 15 to Oct 15, 2027, and Filipino American History Month in October 2027, running into the 2027-28 City Edition season
tentpoles.moment: Heritage months and the 2027-28 launch window
tentpoles.play: Launch the co-designed capsules signed this season: Hecho en el 407, the Los Suns club jacket, Summer Avenue in Memphis, Westside Denver, Desde la Cliff's 2027 build, Ube x Mango in LA and the Bay's Filipino heritage line. Then roll straight into the 2027-28 City Edition pitches: Brooklyn's Kings County, Chicago's 1901 W. Madison, Minnesota's Mill City Lights.

priorities.title: Banner '26: the 1973 bookend, ring night to Christmas (ring-night-1973-2026)
priorities.why: The league's biggest market defends its first title in 53 years. Ring night falls on opening night and the Finals rematch at noon on Christmas, the season's two most visible dates. Only Nike-dressed New York can tell the 1973/2026 story.

priorities.title: Next Chapter: win the jersey wall at the opener (next-chapter-opener)
priorities.why: The NBA's most mythologized brand is resetting its jersey wall around Doncic and Reaves, with no look yet claimed for the era. Every retail tier already exists here, so the opener sets the era's look and volume for years, and a Christmas home game follows.

priorities.title: Earn Philly: stock the debut, save the welcome (earn-philly-home-debut)
priorities.why: A LeBron and Brown superteam in a Specter season is the league's biggest new-arrival opening. Philadelphia's earn-it mechanic, where local pieces wait for wins, is the template for every arrival market.

priorities.title: Giannis arrival season, built on what exists (giannis-305-arrival)
priorities.why: Giannis, confirmed in Miami by the live-verified League Pulse, is the biggest Nike signature star in Heat colors this era. He arrives in a title-or-bust year in a gateway shopping market, and the brief's plan ships now on existing Freak colorways and swingman depth.

priorities.title: Wembanyama youth ladder and sub-$100 tier (wemby-youth-ladder)
priorities.why: San Antonio has a title co-favorite with a Nike global star, an opening-night home game and a family-sized, price-aware region that runs to Mexico. That makes always-on youth depth the highest-volume, lowest-risk bet in the West.

priorities.title: Blazermania 50: the '77-at-50 line, timed to rights (blazermania-50)
priorities.why: The '77-at-50 date is a once-only anniversary in Nike's hometown, and the City Edition slot is empty. Portland is also the home lab, where the Albina co-author model and the rights-sequenced heritage calendar get proven before they go league-wide.

priorities.title: Shift Change: the winter layer program (shift-change-winter)
priorities.why: A 60-win No. 1 seed in a Specter year, with an opening-night home game and a seven-month outerwear season, makes Detroit the strongest mix of contender and winter. It works only if the product speaks Detroit's own knit and shell language, not Carhartt's.

priorities.title: Made on Roosevelt: the locals-first All-Star pop-up (all-star-made-on-roosevelt)
priorities.why: All-Star Weekend, which Phoenix hosts, is the league's one fixed national stage in a single market. A locals-first pop-up that clears licensing in time sets the template for how Nike shows up at every future All-Star.

priorities.title: Raptors Winter Blackout, sold coast to coast (winter-blackout-north)
priorities.why: Canada's only team sells to a whole country through a five-month winter. Its layer program is the league's largest single cold-weather opportunity, and it stays clear of the anti-US mood that hampers loud campaigns.

priorities.title: Cup Fridays into holiday gifting (holiday-and-cup)
priorities.why: Oklahoma City is a 60.5-win-total co-favorite whose star is a Converse athlete, and its fan base is a whole state buying under $100 for families. Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams and Holmgren youth jerseys and state-outline gifts are the efficient volume play through Cup nights and the holidays.

priorities.title: Nor'easter layering system with a snow-emergency drop (noreaster-layering)
priorities.why: Elite loyalty and high-income New England retail meet a $175 tax-free clothing line, a five-month winter and a Christmas home game. Layers sidestep the roster doubt that caps player product after the Brown trade.

priorities.title: Lake Wind: the coat over the jersey (lake-wind-outerwear)
priorities.why: Chicago's global heritage retail engine is already running, so the cold-weather hero coat is the biggest net-new revenue line in a rebuild year. It also anchors the 2027-28 Big Shoulders build.

priorities.title: Mill City Christmas for the OKC home game (mill-city-christmas)
priorities.why: Minnesota hosts the Thunder on Christmas night, anchors the Cup ready-swap template and sits in more league tentpoles than any market without a board item. Both stars wear rival brands, so a Mill City holiday layer sells the city instead.

priorities.title: Clutch Red and Gold heritage line (red-and-gold-clutch-heritage)
priorities.why: The reported 2026-27 red-and-gold throwback (verify) would bring back the 1971-95 memory at lower rights risk than the slab-finish capsule. Houston is a 47.5-win-total market with one of the league's most complete design languages. The item waits on confirmation of the Classic/throwback designation and clearance for Olajuwon's likeness.

priorities.title: 404 / 678 / 770 metro capsule, with a 404 Day chapter (area-code-metro-capsule)
priorities.why: Atlanta is the cleanest proof of 'city before crest': near-top culture, soft team fandom and an MLK Day home game. Its area-code capsule is the prototype for the league-wide Codes template.

portland.title: Travel in three sweeps, not 30 visits
portland.detail: Sweep one, re-baselined to Oct 9-Nov 27 for the opener and the Cup, covers only markets with this-season decoration on in-line blanks: New York, Philadelphia, Los Angeles, Miami, San Antonio, Oklahoma City, Detroit, Portland and the Cup home markets. Sweep two, from MLK Day Jan 18 to All-Star Feb 19-21, covers civic, Specter and heritage programs. Sweep three, May to July, runs 2027-28 co-design sessions. Each sweep has a named owner pair: the Portland market lead plus the regional partner manager. Each also has a fixed market list and a travel budget set as a share of the season's program budget, roughly 40/35/25 across the three. And each has a go/no-go checklist: signed partner agreement, rights cleared, blank stock on hand, a licensed printer slotted. Between sweeps, local partners and licensed printers handle fast-turn, so nobody flies product to a clinch.

portland.title: Run two product clocks and tag every idea
portland.detail: Cut-and-sew, footwear colorways and City Edition pitches run on a 9-18 month clock, so most 2026-27 briefs rightly hold uniforms for 2027-28 or 2028-29. Anything for this season must be decoration on in-line blanks through a 2-6 week quick-turn lane. Tag every product in a market plan 'ships now', 'FW27' or 'uniform cycle' before it reaches a review.

portland.title: One partner model, 30 local casts
portland.detail: Use a standard paid co-author agreement: a fee plus royalty, credit on the hangtag, approval rights and a multi-year term. Add a 'listen first' season where the briefs ask for one (Caribbean Brooklyn, Minnesota's Somali, Hmong and Native communities, Denver's Welton Street and Westside, Albina). Back it with a central rights desk for Converse, Jordan, NBPA, school, HBCU and estate approvals, since a third of the top opportunities wait on clearance.

portland.title: Use Portland as the lab, not the template
portland.detail: Pilot the Albina co-author model, the Big Dark layer program and the 48-hour clinch kit with Portland Gear at home first. Use the league's most Nike-literate crowd as a wear-test and credibility panel. Don't export Portland's insider taste to value-led markets like Oklahoma, Utah or Memphis. There the same system needs simpler graphics and sub-$100 price ladders.

portland.title: Fund by calibrated tier, not market size alone
portland.detail: Tier 1 (league opportunity 75 or higher) is New York, the Los Angeles Lakers, Miami, Philadelphia and San Antonio: full national programs and about 45% of the program budget. Tier 2 (55-74) is Toronto, Oklahoma City, Detroit, Portland, Chicago, Boston, Phoenix, Houston and Minnesota, with about 35%. Run Oklahoma City as a contender on a value ladder, not as a small market. Tier 3 (below 55) gets about 20%, split between the craft-led culture capitals of New Orleans, Atlanta, Brooklyn, DC and Memphis and value programs in Utah, Sacramento, Indiana, Milwaukee and Charlotte. Re-score every market at the Feb 11 trade deadline and after the first round, because the reshuffle showed how fast a face can move.

portland.title: Read league scores as calibrated and brief scores as local
portland.detail: Each brief scores its market on its own terms. The league scores re-calibrate all 30 against each other: about 50 is league average on opportunity, retail and fandom, and culture runs higher (median about 62) because every brief rated its own design well highly. League scores stay within 25 points of the brief, and every score note quotes the brief's numbers so the two read side by side. Culture scores only the depth of distinct local design material. Brand crowding and door quality belong to retail, and opportunity is demand plus Nike's rights position. The priority board ranks by opportunity plus a date bonus: +10 for a once-only date Nike can own in the market, +5 for an opening-night, Christmas or MLK Day home game. Below the cut sit Golden State at 59, Indiana at 58, Cleveland at 55 and Denver at 48. Indiana's Hinkle final is carried by the Cup tentpole.

watchlist.why: On Mar 25, 2026, per the verified league calendar, the Board of Governors voted 30-0 to explore expansion bids from Seattle and Las Vegas for a 2028-29 entry, with reported fees of $7-10B per team. A final vote needs 23 of 30 governors, and no franchise has been awarded. Adam Silver repeated in September that he aims to decide by the end of 2026. Seattle lost the SuperSonics to Oklahoma City in 2008 and keeps their green and gold alive through nostalgia and the Storm, three hours from Portland. Have a Sonics-heritage contingency plan ready in Portland by that end-of-2026 decision: mark rights, Storm and local partners, and careful handling of Oklahoma City's origin story.

The other bid in the verified 30-0 exploratory vote: a 2028-29 target, $7-10B fees and a decision expected by the end of 2026, with reports that Las Vegas may be decided before Seattle. It already hosts Summer League and the Aces, and it held three NBA Cup finals (2023-25) before the 2026 final moved to Hinkle. A fan base there would be built from transplants and tourists, closest to the Sun Belt Arrival Cities cluster. Confirm the ownership group and arena plan once an award is made.

The league has staged regular-season games there and runs the G League's Capitanes. San Antonio's 'Spurs Nation' and the Mavericks' and Suns' Latino bases already reach across the border. Confirm 2026-27 Mexico City games and any NBA Europe or international expansion news before planning a Spanish-first regional line.

watchlist.market: Portland (Moda Center lease) and the Clippers (Aspiration ruling)
watchlist.why: Two existing markets in flux. Portland has $586M in public commitments toward Moda Center upgrades but no signed lease under new owner Tom Dundon. The Clippers play this season with Steve Ballmer suspended for a year, a $30M fine and their 2029-2033 first-round picks taken. The Sept 2 ruling is confirmed in the live-verified League Pulse, though appeals or changes aren't tracked. Confirm the lease status and the Clippers' business-side leadership before committing multi-year partner money in either. The Clippers' league scores don't depend on the ruling.

scores.note: The league ceiling on opportunity, culture and fandom: the biggest market, defending its first title since 1973, with the deepest homegrown basketball, music and art culture. Retail sits just behind the Lakers and Chicago because MSG, Puma's Clyde and Fanatics crowd Nike's lane in the most license-heavy market (brief scores: opportunity 91, culture 96, retail 84, fandom 94).

Second only to New York on opportunity and first on retail: a reset jersey wall in the league's most mythologized brand meets every retail tier. Fandom sits below the true elite this season, on grief over LeBron and a 46.5-win projection (brief scores: opportunity 90, culture 94, retail 88, fandom 86).

Top-three opportunity: Giannis is Nike's biggest signature star, in a gateway shopping market with deep Cuban, Haitian and Latin design material. Fandom is just above average because Miami's crowd runs on playoffs and winning, not lifelong loyalty (brief scores: opportunity 86, culture 92, retail 78, fandom 72).

A LeBron-and-Brown contender in a Specter year gives Philadelphia top-four opportunity and near-elite fandom. Its design material (Philly soul, the mural program, North Fifth Street, Iverson-era street style) is real but less distinct than the top culture band. Thin taste-setting independents and a throwback lane owned by Mitchell & Ness hold retail down (brief scores: opportunity 86, culture 91, retail 68, fandom 85).

A title co-favorite led by Wembanyama, in a one-team region that runs to Mexico, puts fandom and opportunity near the top. Retail is ordinary mall-and-Academy volume, and the Fiesta and West Side culture is distinctive but narrower than the coastal giants' (brief scores: opportunity 82, culture 86, retail 56, fandom 90).

A country-sized market with the Leonard reunion and Nike's own Carter archive sits above average everywhere. CAD pricing, cross-border leakage and post-'Elbows Up' wariness of US brands hold it below the US giants (brief scores: opportunity 78, culture 88, retail 70, fandom 80).

The league's second-most intense fandom and a 60.5-win co-favorite with a Converse-signed star put opportunity in the top ten, scored on demand and Nike's rights position, not doors. Small-metro, value-minded retail and a thinner design well than the culture capitals keep retail and culture below average (brief scores: opportunity 70, culture 66, retail 40, fandom 86).

A 60-win No. 1 seed in a Specter year, a seven-month outerwear season and a deep maker culture lift opportunity, culture and fandom well above average. A thin city-core retail map and unconfirmed partner doors keep retail below the line (brief scores: opportunity 80, culture 90, retail 55, fandom 80).

The six-banner heritage engine and a full flagship-to-mall network put Chicago second in the league on retail and top five on culture. A 31-51 rebuild and a 2027-28 build window hold opportunity and fandom nearer the middle (brief scores: opportunity 82, culture 93, retail 84, fandom 74).

Nike's hometown, a once-only '77-at-50 year, a Lillard-Morant backcourt and intense statewide loyalty lift opportunity and fandom well above average. Few public Nike doors and a Rose Quarter retail desert put retail below it (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 84, retail 56, fandom 80).

Boston has elite heritage fandom and strong New England retail. Roster doubt after the Brown trade and Nike playing away to New Balance and adidas cap opportunity. Its design well is narrower than the Black-led design capitals' (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 84, retail 78, fandom 86).

Hosting All-Star (Feb 19-21) and an under-served Latino base lift opportunity above average. The Valley's Chicano, Indigenous and Van Buren neon material puts culture just below the league median. Retail is around average, and a bubble roster holds fandom below it (brief scores: opportunity 78, culture 82, retail 62, fandom 64).

One of the league's most complete local design languages and a Durant-Sengun playoff team keep culture high and opportunity above average. Car-bound sprawl and an attention war with football, the Astros and the rodeo keep retail near average and fandom below it (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 90, retail 62, fandom 64).

A loud Edwards-Ball team with a Christmas home game, Garnett's retirement and a deep Minneapolis Sound, Mill City and Somali, Hmong and Native design well put opportunity, culture and fandom above average. Both stars wear rival brands, though, and retail is led by suburban malls (brief scores: opportunity 72, culture 84, retail 58, fandom 76).

One of the league's deepest design wells sits on one of its softest fan bases, because Atlanta's pride runs to the city, not the Hawks. Culture is top five, and fandom sits in the bottom quarter (brief scores: opportunity 74, culture 92, retail 64, fandom 52).

Oakland, San Francisco and Asian American lineages put the Bay's design well in the league's top band, and its spending keeps retail high. A 40.5-win total and an open Curry shoe deal hold opportunity and fandom at the league middle (brief scores: opportunity 72, culture 92, retail 78, fandom 70).

Title-or-bust loyalty puts fandom above average. Cleveland's punk, rap, steel and Akron material sits below the league median. A drive-to-the-mall retail map with no sneaker district and a Browns-first fall keep retail below the line and opportunity at it (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 76, retail 48, fandom 72).

A three-time MVP, a 49.5-win total and a long outerwear season keep opportunity close to the pack. A quiet, understated base, an edge-of-metro retail map and a narrower design well than most put Denver just below average (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 68, retail 48, fandom 64).

A Hinkle Cup final and Haliburton's return give a small market near-average opportunity and above-average gym-faith fandom. Value-led, mall-first retail with no destination door sits in the bottom tier (brief scores: opportunity 68, culture 76, retail 45, fandom 72).

Brooklyn's borough culture and New York retail rank high. After 20-62 in a Knicks title year, Nets fandom is the league's second-thinnest, and the real opportunity is a 2027 build (brief scores: opportunity 66, culture 92, retail 72, fandom 40).

DC's go-go, flag and ward culture sits in the league's top third. A 17-65 hangover in a hockey-first, visiting-fan-heavy arena gives it the fourth-softest fandom until Dybantsa proves out (brief scores: opportunity 66, culture 90, retail 58, fandom 44).

A huge metro with Flagg and distinct Oak Cliff and Fair Park languages has average retail scale and design material below the median. A wounded 26-56 fan base and football's grip on the fall put opportunity and fandom in the bottom half (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 70, retail 58, fandom 54).

Memphis's design well (soul, living rap, jookin, sign painting) is in the league's top third. A post-Ja reset in a small, price-conscious metro with no Nike door puts retail second from the bottom (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 88, retail 38, fandom 66).

Penny pinstripes and a large Boricua base give Orlando a real lane, with design material below the median. No national stage, outlet-heavy retail and playoff-gated loyalty keep opportunity, retail and fandom in the bottom half (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 72, retail 58, fandom 56).

The Inglewood-to-SGV footprint gives the Clippers real design material, if below the league median, and LA retail keeps retail above average. A starless post-Kawhi reset in the Lakers' shadow means the league's third-thinnest fandom and a low opportunity score that holds with or without the Aspiration penalties (brief scores: opportunity 60, culture 80, retail 72, fandom 41).

Hive nostalgia is real. But non-Nike faces, one national window and a college-first, mall-and-outlet metro put Charlotte in the bottom fifth on opportunity and fandom and below average on culture and retail (brief scores: opportunity 58, culture 66, retail 52, fandom 50).

Whole-state, family-sized loyalty keeps fandom near the league average. A small metro in a rebuild, with no national stage and a thin boutique layer, sits near the bottom on opportunity, culture and retail (brief scores: opportunity 52, culture 66, retail 40, fandom 68).

Fans who saved the team keep fandom just above average, and Specter is the main national hook. A likely bottom-West season, a value-leaning Valley and a lighter design well than its California neighbors put Sacramento near the floor on the other three axes (brief scores: opportunity 52, culture 63, retail 44, fandom 70).

Life after Giannis in a small, value-minded rebuild gives Milwaukee the league's second-lowest opportunity. Cream City brick and fish-fry Fridays are its main design assets, and fandom stays below average until Jan 28 (brief scores: opportunity 50, culture 70, retail 40, fandom 56).

The starkest split in the league: New Orleans's culture is second only to New York's, but thin retail, a Saints-first city and a 26-56 team put opportunity, retail and fandom at the floor. It's a craft market, not a volume market (brief scores: opportunity 46, culture 96, retail 34, fandom 38).
